utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you got to the Hotel Fontana, could you please tell us: To whom did you report?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Well, as opposed to the first evening when the security detail of General Mladic was waiting for us to give us instructions, how to do and what to do, they were not there that evening, and we continued to work according to our regular schedule for providing security in the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But who issued the assignments as to who would be stationed where and for how long and at what location?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Well, it was up to us to identify shifts. We were trying to pair off men who were getting along well in one shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that the previous night at one point you were both outside and then guarding the inside as well. Was that the same on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you not guard at all the inside?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Well, that previous evening we were guarding only the upper floor where the rooms were. And we guarded the entrance to the Fontana Hotel, the reception desk, and the outer perimeter. Inside, we were guarding the area leading to the stairs, but we were not going upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, did you notice any upper-echelon officers such as General Mladic, General Krstic, or some of the others?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: While I was outside, there was some officers in the salon, in the lounge. The first night I knew whom we were guarding, and the second night I ignored even that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You ignored or did not know who you were guarding?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: We simply didn't know the second night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, did you manage to sleep at all that night?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Very briefly with interruptions while we were standing guard inside. In the lobby you could get some rest, sitting down. But if you were standing guard outside, there was no rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay at the Hotel Fontana during the night of July 12, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: All night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what point in time did you leave the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Earlier than the first day. I couldn't be more precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that would be July 13, then, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who issued the order for you to leave the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: We were given our orders when we came, to provide security in the Fontana Hotel that night, the whole night, and then return to the police. Later in the morning, nobody added anything. And in the morning we were supposed to leave, go back to our headquarters, and get new assignments. We were hoping, in fact, to get some rest after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you return to your headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes, to the police building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you returned, were you alone or did you return with some or all of the others?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Well, all of us returned, but in clusters, in several groups with a dozen of metres between us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that occasion how did you get back to the headquarters, what means?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: As I said, we returned in small groups on foot, three or four men per group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take the same route that you had taken the previous night in getting to the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your way back from the Hotel Fontana, did you notice whether there were any buses or trucks with Muslim men being held in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No. There were no buses. We didn't see anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the evening while you were there guarding the Hotel Fontana, had you learned whether there were any Muslim men in buses or trucks in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, before we move on, when you were at the Hotel Fontana during the night of the 12th going into the morning of the 13th, did you at any point in time patrol the city of Bratunac, be it for personal reasons or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No, if you're asking me about the 12th. On the 11th and the 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you get back to the headquarters on the morning of July 13, 1995, could you please tell us what you did.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: We stayed there very briefly. And we received instructions to go back. Those people who had been in Potocari were to go back and to continue with the same assignments, with the proviso that I knew from the previous day, having heard it from Colonel Jankovic, that we would continue at the same rate tomorrow. He meant the 13th. That was as far as I was concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you said that "we would continue at the same rate," I take it you're referring to you and Colonel Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes. We would be doing the same things, the counting, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us, if you recall, who it was on the morning of July 13, 1995, that issued the instruction to the members of the Bratunac Brigade military police, that is, to continue doing what the members had been doing the previous day.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: At that moment after we had waited for about half an hour, having come from the Fontana Hotel, Momir Nikolic came and said: "You men from Potocari, go there and continue." And the rest stayed assembled there because he was giving them some instructions. I, with my group, left; I didn't hear what they were saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In light of the fact that you had been up close to two days now, or perhaps even longer than that, did you by any chance inform Momir Nikolic that you might need a rest?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No, not that morning. We hinted at it in Potocari. The previous evening when we spoke to him, when he said that we should assemble outside the police headquarters, we protested a little, saying that we were very tired, exhausted in fact. However, he didn't care, and there was nothing much that we could do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I take it you went to Potocari as instructed, correct, on the morning of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes. We used the same vehicle, that truck we had, and we left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall about what time it would have been when you got to Potocari on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact time. It was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in Potocari, did you find Colonel Jankovic there waiting for you?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I did not see him anywhere around when I arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him later on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes. When the first buses arrived and I believe the boarding had already started, around that time I saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice whether any other officers, higher-echelon officers, were there at the time when you arrived? And I'm speaking about officers from the Main Staff or the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I did not see any officers that I knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers there or the MUP, the specials as you put it?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Well, I found the same set of people as previously. When I came, the checkpoint was not empty. All the men and all the officers were there. People were already lined up, ready to release groups towards the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how large was the group on this particular morning, that is, the morning of the 13th of July, in light of the evacuation process that had taken place the previous day?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: There was that group of policemen. Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No -- well, aside from -- I'm speaking of the Muslim women, children, men. How large of a group had remained there over night?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I was not able to see that from the point where I was standing. You could see they were there and that the crowd reached all the way to the barrier. But how far towards Srebrenica the crowd stretched, I was unable to see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice when you arrived whether men had been separated and kept in the same location where you had told us the day before?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: We are talking about the yard of that building. I could not identify. There were members of police sitting in clusters having breakfast. The yard was empty. I didn't go inside the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go by that building and walk around that building and go inside the building to see what, if anything, had happened to any of those Muslim males that had been kept there, either the 12th, overnight, on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I did not pass by. There were none outside the building, and I don't know about the inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I failed to ask you one question with respect to the 12th and that building and the Muslim males that had been separated and placed there. From your location, did you hear any unusual noises that would give you pause that they were being abused in any fashion?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any shots coming from that direction that would give you pause that perhaps some of them were being shot at or killed?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, I believe this might be a good time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. It's the right time for a break. We'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we were on July 13th, 1995. Would you please tell us how long you were in Potocari on that day.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: All day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what you did all day.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: The same assignment like on the previous day, counting the buses and getting the numbers right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that particular day, did you get any further instructions from Colonel Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how was his demeanor on that day? How did he appear to you?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Like on the previous day, I couldn't notice anything. Only at one moment this member of the MUP was nearby. He was doing the same work that we were doing. And he sort of said that we should pay a bit more attention because the numbers did not match. I assumed that he knew the number of MUP members there as well. So he wanted us to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, during that day did you notice any abuse? Did you observe anyone being abused?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice separation going on, as you had the day before?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the separation process, do you know whether anyone was being abused?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the men that were being separated, where were they placed the second day, that is on July 13th?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: In the same yard of that particular building or house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, at some point did you notice whether these men were also being transported out of there?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "later," how long had you been there before you noticed that the men were also being transported out of there?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I do not know precisely. I know that the yard was full, like on the previous day. So there were a lot of people across the street from that house, too. And then after that, they started boarding as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you counting the buses with the men as well on the second day, July 13th?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And didn't you -- did you incorporate your numbers into the figures, as you had done the day before?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Completely the same, like the day before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the men started being transported out, were there still women and children in Potocari on the 13th, also being transported out at the same time?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall for how long this process went on, that is the evacuation of women, children, and men on July 13?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: All day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what time on July 13 you left Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Late in the afternoon, just before dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that day, did you notice what, if anything, Momir Nikolic was doing in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: During the course of the day he came and went several times, so he was not there all the time. I didn't notice any other activities during the day. Towards the very end of that day, at one moment I noticed him. I was right next to him. That was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll talk more about Momir and what he did later on that day. But first, could you please tell us: After you had completed your task with Colonel Jankovic, that is the counting of persons that had been entering these buses, do you recall whether you were given any other instructions or orders?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: From Colonel Jankovic at one point in time, yes, towards the end of all that, the boarding, I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us about what time it was when Colonel Jankovic gave you this other order on July 13th.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: The last buses were boarding then. It was the end. It was at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did Colonel Jankovic instruct you to do?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: He asked me whether I knew whether we, the policemen, had an available vehicle, and I said we did. Because near me was the driver of that police vehicle of ours, the TAM, that is. Then he told me to go with him towards Srebrenica, towards the barrier, so to go in the direction of Srebrenica to see whether there were any people left. Because everything had been over by then. The barrier had been removed. So that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Was anyone else with you?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Only the driver, the truck driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how far you went with the TAM or this vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: We went in the direction of Srebrenica, about 3 or 4 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually get into Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No. Potocari-Srebrenica is perhaps about 10 kilometres. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during this drive, did you find anyone? Did you notice anyone?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes. His assignment was to see whether there were any other people coming in, civilians, whether they were being brought in. There weren't any at the barrier, but we were supposed to tell them if we saw any to come to this same place and to wait there. They should be ready for the buses in the morning, that no one would be left behind, that these buses would come to pick them up, too. Also, we were supposed to tell them not to panic, that there was no need to panic, and that everything would be all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you drove that 3 or 4 kilometres from Potocari toward Srebrenica, did you come across anyone that had been left behind or was -- had remained behind?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us how many and perhaps where.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: As we went along the road, we stopped at a few places where we would see groups of people. For the most part, these were smallish groups of five or ten persons, mostly women. Some people were actually in front of houses, some even entered the houses. We could even see fire. Somebody was inside. We told them what we were supposed to tell them, and my conclusion was that they were watching us silently, uninterested. So we went all the way up, and then we went back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you transport any of these people that you had seen back to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No. No. We followed orders. We told them where they were supposed to wait. We did not take them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall about how many in total you were able to observe during this 3- to 4-kilometre drive that you took from Potocari towards Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: A couple of dozen of people. I don't think there were very many. Some were already moving along. Some were moving in the direction of Potocari, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you returned to Potocari, did you give a report to Colonel Jankovic who had issued this order to you?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did he tell you to do next?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No. He just nodded and he said: "We finished for today."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall what the lighting conditions were at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: It wasn't dark yet, but it was late in the afternoon, just before dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from there once Colonel Jankovic had told you that you were through for the day, could you please describe to us what you did.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Well, after that -- well, Momir Nikolic was there, too. He told us to report yet again, all of us who were there, to report at the police. He emphasised that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please describe to us who Momir Nikolic was with, other than the military police. Did you notice whether he was with anyone?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No. It was basically three or four military policemen. They were busy with some car there, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, before we get to the car, do you recall, off chance, the military police that were with Momir Nikolic, the individuals? Can you recollect who they were?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Colleagues for the most part. I can't remember all their names. I know the driver I went with, but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he there?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: He was with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that driver, what's his name again?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Milan Gvozdenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that there was Momir Nikolic there and there was something to do with a car. First of all, what was the make of the car, if you recall, and the colour?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I remember the colour. As for the make, a Toyota or Mazda, I'm not sure, sky blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was Momir Nikolic trying to do with this car, this Toyota or Mazda that was sky blue in colour?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: As far as I could see, he was trying, with the assistance of the policemen, these colleagues, to start the car, to ignite it. They were trying to get it going, but I didn't look at the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know whose car this was? Who did it belong to?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: At that moment, no. But later on I asked the policemen. When we were going back, I asked them about those details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you learn?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: According to what they said, that car was at the factory where the UNPROFOR base was. I don't know how it was driven out of there, whether it was the owner who drove it out or the soldiers. That I don't know. I cannot say. I cannot say how they got it, and ultimately they did manage to get it going and they took it in the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, what was Momir Nikolic's involvement with this car?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: He's the one who drove it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you see him driving it -- driving away with that car on the evening of the 13th, late afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you ever learn who the owner was, the rightful owner, of that car?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we say that it was not Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No. No, I mean it wasn't him, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, after you left Potocari, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I've already mentioned that he told us to report to the military police at the military police building. When the last bus left, we got into our vehicle and we went towards the police building in that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what were the lighting conditions when you arrived at the police building by the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: You could still see, but it had started getting dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any orders once you returned to that location?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who issued the orders?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Momir was right in front of the police building, and there were a lot of policemen there. I could say that all of them who happened to be there were there by the car. They were watching, and he was among them. Because he had arrived before me in the truck. I don't know how much time before we did. When I came on the truck, I found him there with the policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: A few minutes later he issued an order to us, that all the policemen who had remained, that meant that not everybody was there, not all the policemen were there, that we should get involved in securing the school and the buses, as he said the buses were on the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, prior to getting this order, were you aware that there were men in buses and in the school, for instance, Muslim men from Potocari? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us at what point in time you learned of this detail and from whom.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I found out on that day, the 13th, when they started leaving, when the bus -- when the men started leaving, when the yard was full. In front of it, they started boarding the buses. Then military policemen got involved. They got on to the buses and left on the buses. I found that unusual on that day. I noticed that all these same people returned, because I knew them, as opposed to the other ones that said they were specialists. Very soon they returned with empty buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: When I had enough time, because I had work to do, I walked up to a few of my colleagues and I asked them where it was that they were going, since they managed to return so quickly. I found it strange. The buses would leave with women on the buses, that was the previous day, and when those buses would leave they wouldn't come back for quite a while. They told me that the order was for us to take them to Bratunac. That's where they got them out of the vehicles, at the school. They said that there were people, they didn't say who these people were, that were guarding them down there, and that's why they got back so quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us whether they had informed you who had issued that order, that is, for the men from Potocari on the 13th to be taken to the school?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you inquire who had issued that order?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't inquire, and they didn't say anything on their own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find it strange that here you would have this elaborate process of men boarding the buses in Potocari and then being transported only 10 kilometres away and placed in the school. Did you find that rather strange?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you learned of this, did you in any way inform Colonel Jankovic so at least he would know that the men were being taken to Bratunac, as opposed to what he had represented to them the day before on the 12th, that pursuant to General Mladic's orders they would be accompanying or meeting up with their families?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No. I asked the policemen when I found it strange. I did not ask them who gave them these orders, but I asked why they did not go like they did the previous day in the direction of Kladanj. And they said that for the sake of security, the Potocari checkpoint was supposed to be done and over with. There weren't enough vehicles. They would be there only briefly, vehicles were coming, and then they would go on. It was something I found clear, this explanation of theirs, so I didn't ask anything else. And I did not discuss the issue with Colonel Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, the previous day you said that the men had gone toward or to Kladanj. Do you know for a fact whether they went there or they went toward there?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Not for a fact, but that was my understanding of what they had said, that the women were going and that the men would follow. And I was convinced that that was the way it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the 13th you told us that what caught your attention and what caused you to make this inquiry was the fact that the turnaround period when the men would leave Potocari and then almost immediately the bus would return, did you notice that on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No. And that's because on the 12th the buses -- do you mean the men?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What I'm -- let me rephrase. You were saying something. You wanted -- I don't want to cut you off.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Their buses, those 10 or 15 buses, left toward the end of the day; they did not return anymore. No buses returned, so I was unable to know whether they took a long time or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I think that's the point I wanted some clarification. Now, getting back to where we had left off, that is the evening of the 13th, you got your instructions from Momir Nikolic with respect to providing further security of buses in town, did Mr. Nikolic tell you exactly where you and the others had to report to?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where exactly did he tell you to report?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: For the most part, it was guarding the school, as I said, and the vehicles, the buses, on the streets of the town. Nothing more precise than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he give any explanations as to why the men were there, how long they would be there, and perhaps where their destination was to be?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Not at first. But he told us when we insisted that we were tired, that it was God knows what day running that we were going without sleep, he explained that this mission would take only a short while, that vehicles were already on the way along with men who would take them over for the remaining leg of their trip, and that our assignment would be completed by midnight, and that after that we would be free to take some rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, was your assignment completed by midnight?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, did you go to where you were instructed to go to, that is where the school is and where the buses were located?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how long you were there, you yourself that is.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: All night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "all night," could you please tell us at what point in time you left that location.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Early morning, between 6.00 and 7.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please describe to us what you saw when you first arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Well, along the way, the school building is halfway towards the Fontana Hotel, on the left. I was moving along that road from the brigade command towards the Fontana Hotel. And at the turn-off towards the school building, it was our task, namely the street from the beginning of the high street all the way to the school building, the street was lined with buses. Our task was to guard this stretch of the road. I took the opportunity to visit my house, which was 10 or 15 minutes away. I lived very close to the Fontana Hotel, close to the town hall. I just wanted to drop by, because I had some problems of family nature. And then I thought I would return and resume my tasks immediately. That's what I did. I stayed only 15 minutes. I was away for 15 minutes, including the time it took me to get there and back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you got back -- when you went to the location, could you please tell us what the lighting conditions were then.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: It was already dark. The street lights were on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether you noticed anyone that you recognised.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: As I was going back from my house, I crossed the main street which went from the petrol station to the Fontana Hotel. There were many buses parked outside the town hall, and I noticed members of the Bratunac police standing by the buses. I went on my way. And in front of the MUP headquarters, I was actually moving along that road that leads to the school. The school was on my left. Outside of the MUP headquarters I saw two policemen. I asked them what our plan of work was. He said -- they said there were policemen deployed on both sides of the road. And they said: "Stay with us," which I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were they military police or were they MUP?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: They were military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you walk around that night or did you stay in one place?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: At that point where I stopped, there were three buses which we covered plus one truck. It was also a TAM truck but rather large; it was full. We covered all-in-all about four vehicles. We moved together in a group along the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "we," who are we speaking of?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I mean myself and the other two military policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How close were these vehicles to the school itself?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: 100, 150 metres. I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that street where you were located throughout the night, could you please tell us how close it is to the soccer stadium that's in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: The street along which I came runs at a straight angle towards the street leading to the school building and continues on towards the football stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But could you tell us how close you were to that -- to the entrance where the football stadium is, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: 150 metres, maybe less. 100 to 150.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your location would it have been possible for you to hear shooting coming from the football stadium?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not certain. Could the witness repeat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes, 150 metres. It was close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you know, I'm just trying to get all the details. Well, did you hear of any shooting that was going on that night, coming from that direction that would have led you to believe that killings were going on in the soccer stadium?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear shooting from that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware at that time that there were Muslim men in that stadium?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what special instructions, if any, you had received prior to taking up your position. In other words, along with your order to go and guard the buses, were you ever given any specific instructions as to what you were to do once you were there?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes. As far as the buses were concerned, we were told that the bus drivers were not present, that we were not allowed to open the doors or let anyone in or out. And as far as we were able, we were to keep away all civilians who happened to be around and to take care to prevent any incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, during the night that you were there, did you hear any shootings?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please describe to us from where you were located where the sound of the shooting or shootings were coming from.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: From the point where I was standing, the shots were coming from my right, which is the direction of the school, Vuk Karadzic school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how many shots you believe you heard that particular night, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I couldn't be precise. It was volleys of automatic gunfire. One volley of automatic gunfire. I cannot tell you how long or I cannot tell you even the number of rounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything that you recall happen preceding this volley of rounds of automatic gunfire?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us what you recall you heard prior to the volley of automatic gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Before all this around the middle of the night or perhaps a little later, half an hour and before that and all the way up to when the shooting started, shouts were coming from the direction of the school. Whether they were coming from people standing outside the school building or inside, I couldn't be precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were these shouts about, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Those were male voices shouting, shouting the same thing over and over again. I could even say that it was one and the same voice calling something like: "People from Glogova, where are you? What are we waiting for? Don't you see they're going to kill us all?" And the point was that he was calling them to take some action, resistance maybe. I couldn't tell you the exact words, but that was the point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know what, if anything, happened to this individual?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I know that after the shooting I could no longer hear the shouts. That much is certain: When the shooting was over, the shouting did not continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you know what he was talking about when he said -- when he mentioned "Glogova"? Do you know whether he was referring to any particular incident that might have occurred earlier?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No. There were no incidents. I had no associations whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, during the night did you shoot at anyone?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the two military police that you were with, did they shoot at anyone?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No. No, the place where we were standing was under control. We had absolutely no problems with these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see anyone else, aside from your colleagues that you were with, abusing anyone on that particular night?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a Mr. Bozic by any chance?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Bozic, I don't remember the first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Was there a Mr. Bozic that was a member of the Bratunac Brigade military police?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: There is a Zdravko Bozic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's exactly who I'm referring to, Zdravko.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Although I keep thinking and I remember that there is another Bozic, maybe it's Cvijetin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you saw him that evening?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you see Momir Nikolic that evening?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: He passed by at one point early in the evening before that incident, if we use it as a point of reference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us approximately how long you had been there at your location prior to seeing Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: It must have been between 10.00 and 12.00 when he passed by, around 11.00 maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time did Mr. Nikolic give any particular instructions?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No. He only confirmed what he had said before. Just in passing, informally, he said: "Go on working for a little while longer. You'll get some rest later." He didn't stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you indicated that you were there throughout the whole night and then sometime in the early morning hours you left. Prior to leaving, did help arrive, as had been promised by Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but not in the middle of the night when he promised, but early in the morning, towards dawn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall who these folks were that had come to help out?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I knew them by sight, but I didn't know which unit they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they members of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Certainly not, judging by their uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, speaking of uniforms, could you please assist us. How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: They were wearing black overalls with black bandannas. Some of them were leading hound dogs, German shepherds, on a leash. They were rather rowdy and arrogant. They shouted at the people inside the trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where had you seen these folks before, if indeed you had?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: There was a smaller number of men along the road going from the barrier in uniforms of the same kind. Much fewer than there. I didn't know their faces, but I could see the uniforms were the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now -- but had you -- I believe you said that you had recognised them or by face, you had seen their faces before. And perhaps I misunderstood. Had you seen these folks before someplace?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw the uniforms at the police checkpoint in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know whether they had a commanding officer with them at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes. They had a commanding officer or officers, rather, but I didn't know them. I judged that they were officers because they were giving the other men tasks, telling them what to do, telling them to go on to the buses, that at least one man should go on to each bus. I thought they were officers; maybe I was mistaken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if there was one particular individual that stood out as the person in charge of this particular group?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to going to that location the night before, had Momir Nikolic informed you who your commanding officer would be during the night while you performed those functions?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said that you left sometime in the early morning. Could you please tell us when it was that you left. What was going on at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: When these people were coming, they started boarding the trucks. The drivers were not around at the moment. One or two of these armed persons I shall call them, because I don't know who they were, got on to the buses, and then the vehicles left. There were vehicles standing the whole length of the road between the brigade command and the Fontana Hotel. And then they left along the main road towards the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I didn't do anything. I stayed on. Seven or eight buses had already left. And then it was the turn of the buses and the truck that I was guarding, together with my colleagues, the three buses and one truck. People started boarding them. The buses left. We stayed on a minute longer for the truck to leave as well. And after it was done, our assignment for the night was over and we, too, left to get that rest we had been promised. It was maybe the first time that we did not go first to the police headquarters to report. That was the regular practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when again you reported to work or reported back to the military police headquarters for your next assignment?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was on that same day when we went home, in the morning. When we left there were no buses left, nothing and no one. In the afternoon we found some policemen in the police headquarters, including Mile Petrovic, the deputy commander. I did not see the commander, Mirko, around. Mile Petrovic said there were no particular assignments waiting for us, except that he himself plus another two policemen who had had less work to do in the previous days to do the normal guard duty. He said the rest of us were free. After that, I went back home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any buses there when you returned?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: In the town?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No, not even when I came there and even less when I was leaving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you report to Momir Nikolic what you had seen earlier, that is those armed men with the different uniforms that had a rather rude and obnoxious behaviour?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: After they arrived, I didn't see him anywhere around. And the next day, that afternoon in the police quarters, he wasn't there either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we've heard testimony in this courtroom that sometime thereafter a few -- a month or two months thereafter there was a reburial process going on, where bodies were taken out of certain graves and then redistributed to new sites. Were you in any way involved in that process?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No, not in any way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I just want to go back to the soccer stadium. You told us where you were located in relation to that soccer stadium. Are there any residential apartment buildings near the soccer stadium?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises. The witness is not very distinct when he speaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from the apartment buildings that are near the soccer stadium, would one be able to look into the stadium to see if -- what's happening in the stadium?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: The buildings are very close, but viewed from the other side perhaps about 150 metres. And the sports field is practically in the centre of town and there is a fence around it only. It's about 2 metres tall. So it's not that you have proper seats around it or anything like that. Perhaps there are just a few seats in the direction of Glogova, on that side. So everything can be seen from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so getting back to -- just make sure that I understand your answer correctly. From the apartment buildings looking towards the soccer field, the residents of those apartment buildings would be able to see what is happening in the field itself?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes. They always watch games from their terraces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, assuming - and I know I'm asking you a hypothetical - but assuming that there were some thousand Muslims in that soccer stadium and several officers were there shooting and killing some of those Muslim men that were there with automatic rifles, with their hand pistols, and what have you, do you think that you would have heard and noticed those events from where you were located?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Well, if I heard those shouts from the right side, of course I would have heard them from the left side, too, not to mention shooting and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, have you heard what happened to the men that left -- that were in those buses and left Bratunac? Did you hear what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not speaking whether you heard what happened to them back then, but afterwards, later on. Did you ever learn where those people ended up?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Well, the media indicated that most of these people were killed, but I will not be the judge of that. I believe that the truth will come out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you see any killings while you were there?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, how is it possible that you didn't know that those people were about to be killed, in light of your close proximity to them for the two days, the 12th and the 13th, and in light of what you were able to see and observe? Do you have an explanation?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the proximity that you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you were in Potocari on the 12th and the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One may draw the conclusion that because you were there, because you had seen the men being separated, because you had seen the women, children, and men being transported out of there, that it would stand to follow, logically speaking, that you would also know the fate of the men.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No, no. I could not have even thought of any such thing, that something like that had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Colonel Jankovic at any point in time give you the impression that he knew what would happen to the men?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No. I believe that I could have noticed something like that from his behaviour, but as much as I got to know him as a person and as an officer over this brief period of time, he behaved in a correct manner. He seemed sincere to me, and I did not suspect him in any way of having participated in any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I want to show you what has been introduced into evidence as D164. It's a report from Colonel Jankovic to the command of the Drina Corps, intelligence department. It was sent July 14, 1995, 30 minutes into July 14, 1995. If you could look at that last paragraph where it says "PS," the very last paragraph. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please read that. Read that to yourself and I will be asking you. And for the record let me read it. It says: "I think if we want to take over the enclaves of Zepa and Gorazde in the same way, it will be necessary to present the operation in Srebrenica in the media, so as to show that we had rendered adequate treatment to the civilians, and even to soldiers who surrendered their weapons." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you characterise the treatment of civilians while you were there in front of Colonel Jankovic to have been adequate?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly as far as he was concerned, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in looking at this, can you draw any conclusions as to whether Colonel Jankovic himself as of 0030 hours into 14 July 1995 was aware of what was to happen to any men?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, he's asking the witness for a conclusion, and we would submit that that's not appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think we could arrive at certain conclusions when we read this paragraph at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well, Your Honour. I just have a couple more questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in Potocari, did you notice whether any food and water was being distributed to the civilian population that was there?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was any food distributed to you? Were you able to get some of that bread and canned goods and water that was being offered?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: We tried, but we didn't get anything. Food was being distributed by the quartermasters of our brigade. They had the same type of vehicle, a TAM. There was a lot of bread slices that were cut into four pieces, and there was pate in tins. They took this to the buses and to the people who were behind their backs in the yard, because they were standing in the street on the road. We reacted at one moment, asking them to give us some, too. Even the specialists asked for food; however, they refused. They said that the orders were that the food was only for the people who were being transported. Before that, I noticed General Mladic near them, too. I did not hear what he was saying, but I did see that he was yelling at them trying to explain something with his hands and arms, probably directing them to do this or that, but I don't know. I'm not sure. They said that they had received orders to the effect that the food was only for them, so it was my assumption that this was his order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And just finally, you told us that on the 14th in the afternoon you reported. That's when you saw, I believe, Mr. Petrovic. And after that --

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that day, did you go right back to work?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: No. As I have already said, some people would stay to provide security for the building and the rest of us were off and we could go and get some rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I take it you were off?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I left, although even before I came there I had health problems. After that, due to exhaustion, my fluid levels went down. I cannot claim whether it was on the 15th or on the 16th that I reported at the Bratunac clinic, and that's where I was treated. I'm just not sure of the day, whether it was the 15th or the 16th. I was at home, and then I got these infusions or whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very, very much, sir. I have no further questions. Perhaps Mr. Stojanovic, who represents Mr. Jokic, may have some questions. I'm sure the Prosecutor will, and perhaps even the Judges. I want to thank you for being frank and complete with me. And if you could be as equally frank and complete with them, I would most appreciate it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Janjic. Good afternoon, Your Honours. In view of everything he said in the cross-examination today, we do not have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, it's time for the break. Witness, as I said to all the witnesses before, that during your stay in The Hague you can still under oath, so do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. We will continue tomorrow. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The hearing for today is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
